new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Contrastive stress occurs on the first and second syllables. 'hije 'sit' 'guome 'die' 'rihuve 'to be sweet' hi'je 'uncle' guo'me 'Spanish moss' ri'huve 'carry over the shoulder' [p. 4:] Phonemic stress is not written.

new_statements.locator: p. 3, section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)'; also p. 4, 'Conventions: Orthographic'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: 5 pp., text layer present, Acrobat PDFMaker 2004). extracted text page 3 shows, under the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', the single line 'Contrastive stress occurs on the first and second syllables.' followed by the three minimal pairs exactly as quoted ('hije 'sit' / hi'je 'uncle'; 'guome 'die' / guo'me 'Spanish moss'; 'rihuve 'to be sweet' / ri'huve 'carry over the shoulder'). Page 4 under 'Conventions: Orthographic' reads 'Phonemic stress is not.' Both locators correct; wording verbatim. No other stress, tone, length or pitch statement anywhere in the sheet (a full-text search for stress/accent the full text layer: the only other hit is the example word 'tone' = 'axe')…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog codes Omie as lexical (unpredictable) stress on the strength of Austing & Upia 1975 p. 517 ('Stress is contrastive.. hije: grandparent / hi:je sit'). The OPD agrees that stress is contrastive and adds a constraint: the contrast is confined to the first versus the second syllable, with three minimal pairs (the 'hije' pair matches the 1975 pair). Same type, more detail, no contradiction.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is phonemic (contrastive): it falls on either the first or the second syllable of the word and its position is not predictable from the segmental shape, as shown by three minimal pairs (initial vs. second-syllable stress in two- and three-syllable words). The orthography does not mark it. Nothing is said about tone or length despite the section heading.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The statement confines the contrast to syllables 1 and 2; no example shows stress beyond the second syllable, so a stress placed later than the second syllable is not attested in this sheet.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD covers Ömie (Aomie) [AOM] of Afore, Kokoda, Oro Province, villages Enjoro, Asapa, Ehoro, Godibehi, Savarihambo, Gorabuna, Kero, Gora; no dialect is singled out. Dutton 1969 uses the name Aomie for the same language.
